object_description: three staggered building volumes parallel to the street
design_condition: The staggered volumes are set back and aligned with the topography to preserve visual axes, retain existing trees and villas, and create a flowing sequence of courtyards and open spaces between old and new buildings.

positive.statement: The placement and staggering reduce the spatial impact while establishing a dialogue with the historic buildings.
The spatial expansion creates a well-proportioned sequence of squares that connects lower and upper levels.
The typological separation of the buildings leads to a clear allocation of functions.
Despite the considerable depth of the building, the sectional solution allows all rooms to be adequately naturally lit.
Separating the public wing from the workshop halls prevents noise and other emissions from spreading into public spaces.
The large spans enable very flexible room design on the upper floors.
The construction concepts suggest economical and sustainable execution.
The project has an architectural expression that is pleasantly appropriate to the task and location.

negative.statement: The demarcations toward the main street appear too pragmatic and hardly strengthen the desired address.
The proposed steps place an unpleasant strain on the entrance situation and historic courtyard.
The design in the western area remains rudimentary, with no design discussion in the historic context.
The tree species composition must necessarily be limited to native plants.
The simple fire-protection approach does not meet the regulations in all respects.
